applies_why: The judge text counts Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 toward a broken link, which triggers K-G4's requirement to quote the earlier-round sentence pressing them and name that round.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: Phrase: 'A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way.' Reading 1: using Matthew 1:18/25 as proof of the broken link counts them under K-G4. Reading 2: stating the link is broken does not itself count any cited-in verse as an unanswered witness.
why: The judge text uses Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 as support for a broken link but does not quote the earlier-round sentence pressing them or name any round, so it breaches K-G4.
